legend: A permutation of size N$$$N$$$ is a sequence of N$$$N$$$ positive integers containing the numbers 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$ where each number appears exactly once in the sequence. For example, [1,4,5,3,2]$$$[1,4,5,3,2]$$$ is a permutation of size 5$$$5$$$, while [1,1,4,3,5]$$$[1,1,4,3,5]$$$ and [1,6,2,3,4]$$$[1,6,2,3,4]$$$ are not.

We can compare two permutations using lexicographical order. For two permutations p$$$p$$$ and p$$$p$$$ of the same size N$$$N$$$ where p=[a1,a2,...,aN]$$$p = [a_1,a_2,...,a_N]$$$ and q=[b1,b2,...,bN]$$$q = [b_1,b_2,...,b_N]$$$, we define p$$$p$$$ is smaller than q$$$q$$$ if and only if there exists an index i$$$i$$$ such that aj=bj$$$a_j=b_j$$$ for every j<i$$$j \lt i$$$ and ai<bi$$$a_i \lt b_i$$$. For example, [1,3,4,2,5]$$$[1,3,4,2,5]$$$ is ordered before [1,3,5,2,4]$$$[1,3,5,2,4]$$$.

Two permutations p$$$p$$$ and q$$$q$$$ of size N$$$N$$$ are considered an ideal pair if, when all N!$$$N!$$$ permutations of size N$$$N$$$ are arranged in a circle based on lexicographic order, permutation p$$$p$$$ and permutation q$$$q$$$ are positioned directly opposite each other in the circle.
Given a permutation p$$$p$$$, your task is to identify the permutation q$$$q$$$ that together forms an ideal pair.
input: The first line contains one integer N$$$N$$$ (2≤N≤1,000,000)$$$(2\le N \le 1,000,000)$$$ — size of the permutation.
The second line contains N$$$N$$$ distinct integers from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$ — the given permutation p$$$p$$$.
output: One line contains N$$$N$$$ distinct integers that are the permutation that forms an ideal pair with permutation p$$$p$$$.
